title: Which traveller suits the desert, the snow, deep water and space?
description: Tanvi has four picture cards of places. The video matches each place to the traveller or vehicle that suits it.
teaching_notes: One idea: the place decides the traveller. Watch for children who pick one favourite vehicle for every place.

source: Which would be used to travel (a) in a desert, (b) in a snow
video_script.why: The child has met old and new ways to travel but has not yet matched a place to a suitable traveller.
video_script.substitution: Look at what the ground or the air is like, then pick the traveller that suits it.
video_script.anchor: Tanvi's four picture cards pinned on her classroom wall in Pune
video_script.wrong_answer: ride my bicycle in all four places
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu says he will ride a bicycle in all four places. Wheels sink in sand, slide on snow, and cannot go under water or into space.
video_script.payoff_line: a camel, a yak, a submarine and a spacecraft

final_answer.value: (a) camel, (b) yak, dog or reindeer, (c) submarine, (d) spacecraft
final_answer.spoken: a camel for the desert, a yak, a dog or a reindeer for snow, a submarine under water, a spacecraft for outer space

hold_back: (a) camel, (b) yak, dog or reindeer, (c) submarine, (d) spacecraft
never_show: a bicycle marked as right for any place
maths_rules: four places: desert (a), snow covered region (b), deep under water (c), outer space (d)
(a) camel; (b) yak, dog or reindeer; (c) submarine; (d) spacecraft
slip: one vehicle for every place ignores what the ground or the air is like
your turn: crossing a wide river long ago; the answer, a boat, is never shown
video_script.design: One idea: the place decides the traveller. Wrong idea: one favourite vehicle for all. The four picture cards stay in the anchor band; the four places are lit one at a time.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; four picture cards sit on a wall: sand, snow, deep water, outer space; a question mark waits under each

marks.m1: the small title card From your book appears
marks.m2: four picture cards appear on a classroom wall
marks.m3: the four cards light up in turn: sand, snow, deep water, outer space
marks.m4: a question mark appears under each card

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Tanvi has four picture cards pinned on her classroom wall in Pune.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>One card shows a desert, one a snow covered hill, one deep water, and one outer space.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Which would be used to travel in each place?

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still and gets an accent underline

marks.m5: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='m5'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

beats.on_screen: the four places come to the stage one by one with a few words under each: soft sand, deep snow, deep water, no air

marks.m6: the four place cards slide to the stage
marks.m7: the sand card glows with the words soft sand, little water
marks.m8: the snow card glows with the words deep snow, steep hill
marks.m9: the water card glows with the words far below
marks.m10: the space card glows with the words no air
marks.m11: all four cards hold, with an empty traveller frame under each

narration: <bookmark mark='m6'/>Look at the four places, one by one.
<bookmark mark='m7'/>The first is hot sand that goes on for many days of walking, with very little water.
<bookmark mark='m8'/>The second is thick snow on a steep hill.
<bookmark mark='m9'/>The third is deep water, far below the waves.
<bookmark mark='m10'/>The fourth is outer space, where there is no air at all.
<bookmark mark='m11'/>Each place needs a traveller that suits it.

beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows a bicycle over all four place cards; a wheel sinks into the sand card; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.m12: Chintu's bubble appears with a bicycle over all four cards
marks.m13: a wheel sinks into the sand card
marks.m14: a wheel slides on the snow card; the water and space cards show a cross
marks.m15: the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='m12'/>I will ride my bicycle in all four places, because I know it well.
<bookmark mark='m13'/>Think about soft sand. The wheels would sink.
<bookmark mark='m14'/>In deep snow they would slide, and a bicycle cannot go under water or into space.
<bookmark mark='m15'/>Each place needs its own kind of traveller.

beats.on_screen: the empty frames under the sand and snow cards fill in: a camel, then a yak, a dog and a reindeer

marks.m16: a camel appears under the sand card
marks.m17: the words soft sand, little water light up beside the camel
marks.m18: a yak, a dog and a reindeer appear under the snow card
marks.m19: the words strong, cold light up beside them

narration: <bookmark mark='m16'/>For the desert, people have used camels.
<bookmark mark='m17'/>A camel can walk on soft sand and go for days with little water.
<bookmark mark='m18'/>For the snow covered hill, people have used yaks, dogs and reindeer.
<bookmark mark='m19'/>They are strong, and they can carry or pull loads in the cold.

beats.on_screen: the empty frames under the water and space cards fill in: a submarine, then a spacecraft; a line lists all four

marks.m20: a submarine appears under the water card
marks.m21: the submarine dips below a wave line
marks.m22: a spacecraft appears under the space card
marks.m23: the four travellers glow together in a row

narration: <bookmark mark='m20'/>Deep under water, people use a submarine.
<bookmark mark='m21'/>A submarine is a ship that can go below the water.
<bookmark mark='m22'/>To reach outer space, humans use a spacecraft.
<bookmark mark='m23'/>That gives a camel, a yak, a submarine and a spacecraft, one for each place.

beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the four cards; two lines appear: the place decides the traveller; each place has its own kind; then a new picture of a wide river and an empty box

marks.m24: the line the place decides the traveller appears
marks.m25: the line each place needs its own kind appears
marks.m26: a wide river appears with an empty box

narration: <bookmark mark='m24'/>The place decides the traveller.
<bookmark mark='m25'/>Sand, snow, deep water and space each need a different kind of traveller.
<bookmark mark='m26'/>Your turn. Long ago, how would people have crossed a wide river?
